Sure! If you want to see what’s on your **C:** drive from the command line, you can use the `dir` command. Here’s how you’d do it:

```cmd
C:\> dir C:\
```

That will list all files and folders in the root of the C drive. If you want to see everything recursively (including sub‑folders), add the `/s` switch:

```cmd
C:\> dir C:\ /s
```

If you’re on PowerShell, you can use `Get-ChildItem` instead:

```powershell
PS C:\> Get-ChildItem -Path C:\ -Recurse
```

Feel free to let me know if you’d like help filtering the results (e.g., only show `.txt` files) or if you want to save the output to a text file.
